title: Critical behavior of the driven Curie-Weiss model
authors: Ruohan Xu, Faezeh Khodabandehlou, Christian Maes
abstract: We complete the phase diagram of the macroscopic Curie-Weiss magnet in a time-periodic external field, as a function of temperature and driving parameters. There is a regime (large enough driving amplitude and frequency, at low temperatures) where stable paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases coexist. In particular, we present a new detailed analysis of the (nonequilibrium) specific heat, diverging at the same critical inverse temperature $β_c$ as the magnetic susceptibility. The new Curie temperature decreases with the driving, and we find critical exponent $α=1$ for $β\downarrow β_c$, and $α\simeq 0.86$ for $β\uparrow β_c$, even for small driving. A Floquet analysis shows the nature of the criticality, which is dynamical, with implications that remain unseen and are mostly impossible when the system is in thermal equilibrium.
summary: This paper investigates the non-equilibrium thermodynamics of a driven Curie-Weiss magnet, mapping out its full phase diagram under time-periodic fields. Key findings include the observation of dynamical criticality, where specific heat diverges with different exponents depending on the direction relative to the critical temperature. The work demonstrates that external driving fundamentally alters both the nature and quantitative description of magnetic phase transitions.
main_problem: The study focuses on completing the phase diagram and analyzing the critical behavior of a Curie-Weiss magnet when subjected to a time-periodic external driving field.
main_result: The system exhibits dynamical criticality, with specific heat diverging at different exponents ($\alpha=1$ vs $\alpha\simeq 0.86$) depending on whether the inverse temperature is approaching or receding from the critical point.
method: The analysis employs mean-field theory combined with non-equilibrium calorimetry (AC-calorimetry) and linear response theory to calculate thermodynamic quantities like specific heat and susceptibility.
model_or_system: The model is the Curie-Weiss magnet described by a kinetic Ising model in mean-field approximation, subjected to an external field $h_0(t) = \delta_0 + A_0 \cos(\omega t)$. The dynamics are governed by a relaxational stochastic equation for magnetization $m(t)$.
key_observables: Specific heat ($C$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), and time-averaged magnetization $\langle m angle$.
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), driving amplitude ($A$), and driving frequency ($\omega$). The critical point $ eta_c$ shifts due to the drive.
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on approximations such as the near-quasistatic ansatz for AC-calorimetry, or perturbative expansions in small parameters like $A$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate specific heat divergence vs. $ eta$ under varying driving parameters; they also compare contributions to heat capacity divergence in first-order versus second-order transition regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the phase diagram, derives equations for magnetization and response functions using mean-field theory, calculates $C$ via AC-calorimetry, and determines $\chi$ using linear response theory across different parameter regimes.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how non-equilibrium driving fundamentally alters critical phenomena, yielding exponents and phase boundaries inaccessible in standard thermal equilibrium treatments.
